ratings_why.fun: Voting the water each turn against the board you can scout is a real, readable decision, and Mills and Kobus make every Vote grow something, but mid-fight sinking will take a clear waterline to feel fair.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because one public dial changes both boards at once and makes a unit's Health-to-Attack shape matter; no tribe today acts on the enemy's whole board through a shared number.

verdict_why: Every card now reads in one pass and the fantasy shows in the play; what is left is tuning and UI, which more revision would only make different.

points.text: Board Almoner reads your Level while Under reads the water (both Levels plus Floods); two near-identical thresholds will get mixed up. A distinct icon on the gauge for 'your Level' versus 'the water' would help.

Stretch-Holder adds your Level, but the water also adds the opponent's Level and Floods, so its neighbours are not always above it as the High Water build says. Fine as a card; the build text oversells it.

Keeper of the Overflow lets a Lowering Board flood too, so Lower pays gold, stats and water while Raise pays mainly Schouw-Walker. Worth giving Raise one more direct payoff so the vote stays a real choice.
Kees Kowk targeting Under enemies against an enemy Diving coot (attacked only if no other target) needs one line on which rule wins in the mirror.
The flavour lands in what cards do: Lower pays gold like drained land, coots dive into the ditch, Tiddy Mun drowns. Lean on that with sunk units visibly under the waterline in the fight view.

standouts.why: Ditch Coot is two words and a Flood: a coot that wants the water, the tribe's idea in one small card.
Tiddy Mun reads cleanly and pays off the drowning fantasy as the marsh spirit should.
Master of the Nine Mills pays for any Vote either way, so every build has a clear capstone.

weakest.why: Bram Stuw is a plain extra Vote that Hendrika does better; little to read or feel.
Schouw-Walker's 'lowest-Health other unit' is fine but generic, and it is nearly the only Raise payoff.
Sluiswacht is a slight gold drip with little of the sluice-keeper's character in it.

flags.note: Overflow never resets, so a long Drain game can start every fight deep underwater.
Gauge-Keeper fed tall plus Tiddy Mun can drown a whole enemy board at Start of Combat.
'Goes Under' fires on every rise and every hit; Rafting Coot and Winter Raft need trigger feedback players can follow.
